prompt: Assuming it is set up correctly, what can you say about a BIND server that has the line "allow-transfer {10.23.98.102; 10.202.79.121;};" in your /etc/named.conf file?
choices: It is a caching-only server with no zones of its own.
It forwards all queries to two upstream servers.
It is a master or slave that allows zone transfers to two other computers.
It blocks all queries from those two IP addresses.
explanation: The allow-transfer directive lists the hosts permitted to request zone transfers, so this server is a master or slave allowing transfers to those two computers.
